audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Quinn/Quinn/Skill/Skill/Quinn/Quinn — Level 1 and Levels 4-5/6 marked even, and the 2+ item row given to Quinn.
audit.why: 54.69% over 512 games and the packet chart is Quinn rows 0-5, Vladimir row 6. The page's own prose says Vlad is one of the weakest level 1s and that two items flips it hard, so both ends of the chart contradicted the text.
audit.corrected: Quinn rows 0-5, Vladimir row 6, both layers.

audit.why: Spikes are right: Quinn owns Lvl 1-3 and the first-item window, Vlad's takeover is Rylai's plus 2 items. Sanguine Pool coming online at level 2 is the real early gate and is already reflected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool was named everywhere but never quantified, and the Grievous Wounds requirement — the single interaction that decides extended trades — appeared only as a passing clause in the item line.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and grants 2 seconds of untargetability, so at rank 1 a baited Pool leaves a 28-second hole; that is the all-in window. Transfusion (Q) and Hemoplague (R) both heal him, so anti-heal timing, not raw damage, determines who wins a long trade.
audit.corrected: Pool is 28s at rank 1 and only 16s maxed, 2s untargetable — bait it then commit; and get Grievous Wounds up before the all-in or Transfusion refills him.
sources: enemyKit W cooldown and untargetable flag

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d under 'Stack pure HP vs %damage' was template filler about burning your own cooldown; dosFull[2].d under 'Build MR + anti-heal' described baiting Pool instead.
audit.why: Both bodies were copied from unrelated slots and say nothing about their own headings.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal body for the anti-heal entry; an MR-over-HP body for the itemisation don't.
